candidates.original_title: Coadministration of a tumor-penetrating peptide enhances the efficacy of cancer drugs
candidates.description: Coadministration of iRGD peptide with DOX increases DOX accumulation in tumor tissue in mice bearing orthotopic 22Rv1 prostate tumors
candidates.citation_sentence: This experiment is similar to what was reported in Figure 2B of Sugahara et al. (2010).
candidates.notes: Replication found no significant effect (p=0.737); effect was in opposite direction from original (Glass' Δ = −0.32 vs 7.41). DOX accumulation in DOX+iRGD group was 0.86 times the DOX+PBS group, compared to ~7.15 times increase in the original. [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Coadministration of a tumor-penetrating peptide enhances the efficacy of cancer drugs
candidates.description: Coadministration of iRGD peptide with DOX reduces tumor weight in mice bearing orthotopic 22Rv1 prostate tumors
candidates.citation_sentence: This experiment is similar to what was reported in Figure 2C of Sugahara et al. (2010).
candidates.notes: Replication found no significant difference in tumor weights (ANOVA p=0.233; pairwise DOX+PBS vs DOX+iRGD p=0.826). Original reported ~0.35g for DOX+iRGD vs ~0.82g for DOX+PBS; replication found 0.668g for DOX+iRGD vs 0.721g for DOX+PBS. [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Coadministration of a tumor-penetrating peptide enhances the efficacy of cancer drugs
candidates.description: Coadministration of iRGD peptide with DOX does not cause body weight loss in mice bearing orthotopic 22Rv1 prostate tumors
candidates.citation_sentence: This is similar to what was reported in Supplementary Figure 9A of Sugahara et al. (2010), except only the 1 mg/kg dose of DOX conditions were tested.
candidates.notes: Replication found no significant body weight shift (ANOVA p=0.217). Original also found no shift at 1 mg/kg dose; shift was only observed at 3 mg/kg. Both original and replication null for this dose. [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]

candidates.original_title: Coadministration of a tumor-penetrating peptide enhances the efficacy of cancer drugs
candidates.description: Coadministration of iRGD peptide with DOX increases TUNEL staining (apoptosis) in tumor tissue in mice bearing orthotopic 22Rv1 prostate tumors
candidates.citation_sentence: This experiment is similar to what was reported in Figure 2D of Sugahara et al. (2010) except that this replication attempt was restricted to the 1 mg/kg DOX conditions.
candidates.notes: Replication found no significant difference in TUNEL staining (ANOVA p=0.282; pairwise p=0.670). Original reported ~1.4x increase for DOX+PBS and ~2.6x increase for DOX+iRGD vs untreated; replication found 0.79x and 0.71x relative to PBS. No detectable TUNEL staining in heart tissue in replication, contrasting original. [ling26: extra entry, not in the external record]
